slide_01_net_two_zones.title: Net additions in the Tambopata buffer zone fell 90% in 2019–21
slide_01_net_two_zones.subtitle: Net mining additions, ha/yr · Tambopata buffer zone (orange) vs Amarakaeri buffer zone (green) · 2010–2025 · Tambopata 1,640 → 163, Amarakaeri 289 → 574 (2016–18 → 2019–21). Thick bars and numbers at the top: period means.
slide_01_net_two_zones.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting on one zone registry (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; corridor = D.L. 1100). Both buffer zones whole (official SERNANP polygons). Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_02_parts_two_zones.title: Pits going out of use made 25%–47% of the fall, most of it in 2019
slide_02_parts_two_zones.subtitle: Net mining additions and their parts, ha/yr, period means · Tambopata buffer zone vs Amarakaeri buffer zone · Tambopata 2016–18 → 2019–21: new land 2,017 → 1,061, stopped 721 → 1,413 (2.0×). Stopped land makes 25%–47% of the fall (four ways of counting map flicker); 68% of the extra stopping is in 2019.
slide_02_parts_two_zones.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting on one zone registry (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; corridor = D.L. 1100). New land = mined for the first time since 1985; re-mined = mined again after a gap; stopped = left the mining class. Net = new + re-mined − stopped. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_03_lapampa_parts.title: New pits kept opening in 2019; pits stopped where the patrols were
slide_03_lapampa_parts.subtitle: Net mining additions and their parts, ha/yr · La Pampa sector (the target) · 2016–2022 · 2019: new land 1,533 (2018: 1,835), stopped 1,495, net 243. Shaded: 2019–21.
slide_03_lapampa_parts.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting on one zone registry (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; corridor = D.L. 1100). New land = mined for the first time since 1985; re-mined = mined again after a gap; stopped = left the mining class. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_04_moved.title: Mining moved across the road; the department never fell
slide_04_moved.subtitle: Net mining additions (and parts), ha/yr · left: corridor across the road, 2010–2025, 60 → 395 (2016–18 → 2019–21) · right: Madre de Dios 3,610 → 4,639 → 12,047 (2016–18 → 2019–21 → 2022–25).
slide_04_moved.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting on one zone registry (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; corridor = D.L. 1100). Right: zones inside the department; they sum to the total. Legality is by location; the map class can't tell legal from illegal. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_05_later_old_pits.title: It came back on old pits: 46% of added land was re-mined
slide_05_later_old_pits.subtitle: Net mining additions and their parts, ha/yr · Tambopata buffer zone · 2010–2025 · later years (2022–25): re-mined 1,139/yr, new land 1,345/yr; without the 2023 spike year re-mined 617/yr (33%).
slide_05_later_old_pits.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting on one zone registry (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; corridor = D.L. 1100). New land = mined for the first time since 1985; re-mined = mined again after a gap; stopped = left the mining class. 2023 is a MapBiomas-only spike (GLAD alerts and Amazon Mining Watch are flat): read 2022–25 with and without it. MAAP #193 (2023) reports miners back on degraded land. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_06_reserve.title: 2025: mining inside the reserve jumped 241 ha after the navy left
slide_06_reserve.subtitle: Net mining additions, ha/yr · Tambopata National Reserve (inside the reserve, not the buffer zone) · 2011–2025 · 2019–21 mean −33/yr; mining area 2025: 777 ha. Navy left the Malinowski River posts in 2025 (MAAP #241, 2026).
slide_06_reserve.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting on one zone registry (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; corridor = D.L. 1100). Platform check: 777 ha of mining inside the reserve in 2025 (protected-area statistics). MAAP #241 (Pacsi et al., 2026) reports ~500 ha inside the reserve, late 2025 to Feb 2026. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_07_causal.title: Did Mercurio cause the fall? Only conditionally, in hectares only
slide_07_causal.subtitle: Estimated change in net mining additions and its parts, ha/yr · Tambopata buffer zone · 2019–21 vs before · causal only if the comparison zones show what Tambopata would have done; upper bound (spillovers, peak at targeting); coincides with COVID. Right: placebo ranks.
slide_07_causal.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 rasters, national buffer-zone panel on the v3 registry (15 zones with pre-2019 mining; scaled ranks: 7 zones above 10 ha/yr). 2×2 = Tambopata minus Amarakaeri, 2019–21 vs 2014–18; M1 = zone + year effects 2014–25; synthetic DiD = own weights (peru_sdid.py, net only). Parts add up to net for the linear estimators.

slide_b1_stopped_split.title: Stopped land: often water, often mined again within 2 years
slide_b1_stopped_split.subtitle: Stopped land (left the mining class), share by what it became and share mining again within 2 years, period means · four zones · 2016–18, 2019–21, 2022–25 (small numbers under the bars: stopped ha/yr). Numbers on top: share mining again within 2 years.
slide_b1_stopped_split.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting on one zone registry (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; corridor = D.L. 1100). Back within 2 years = classifier flicker or re-entry; the last two years cannot be followed up. No image validation sample (plan v3, V3-5).

slide_b2_twins.title: Twins: Tambopata at 16%–41% of their pace; trends differed before
slide_b2_twins.subtitle: Left: mining area (stock), index 2018 = 100, 2010–18 (pre-trends rejected, p < 0.001). Right: Amazon Mining Watch new area 2019–21 per year, % of own 2018 area: a different measure, not net additions.
slide_b2_twins.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Col 4 rasters, v3 registry (Tambopata) / MapBiomas Amazonía Col 6 (twins); Amazon Mining Watch new area, area-weighted (comparable to first-time mining, not net). Twins chosen by fixed rules (rule R*, control_select.py). Different collections: compared as indices, never subtracted.

slide_b3_context.title: Enforcement money peaked in 2019 and faded; gold rose 2.7-fold
slide_b3_context.subtitle: Same years in each panel · PP 0128 executed spending, Madre de Dios (lower bound) · gold price, nominal · net mining additions, La Pampa sector, ha/yr · 2012–2025. Shaded: 2019–21. Context, not a test.
slide_b3_context.source: Source: MEF Consulta Amigable, PP 0128 devengado, Madre de Dios; World Bank Pink Sheet (nominal gold price, annual mean); MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting on one zone registry (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; corridor = D.L. 1100). Correlation not shown: 11 years, and money follows mining.
